lecture_title: Weak Interactions, Virial Corrections, and Inexact Differentials

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: The nonlinear response curve and marked local interval are unobstructed and directly support the calibration discussion; nearby candidates either show less of the curve or more lecturer intrusion.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: A smooth response is linear over a sufficiently limited range.
assets.caption_hint: local linear calibration on a nonlinear thermometer response

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: The board clearly shows the three-dimensional pair-potential integral and its definition as U0, matching the adjacent dimensional interpretation.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Call the integrated strength of the potential U0.
assets.caption_hint: definition and units of the integrated pair strength U0

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: The full kinetic-plus-pair Hamiltonian and both Boltzmann factors are visible with minimal obstruction, improving on the earlier cropped source frame.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The other term is the potential energy.
assets.caption_hint: interacting Hamiltonian and kinetic-configurational Boltzmann factors

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: The board isolates the ideal-gas factor and the normalized configurational integral at the point where the partition function is factorized.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Multiply and divide by the ideal position-space volume factor.
assets.caption_hint: factorization of Z into Z0 and a configurational correction

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: The selected board state contains the leading one, the pair sum, the spectator-volume factors, and the completed first-order correction without the occlusion present in nearby frames.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: There are N times N minus one over two distinct pairs.
assets.caption_hint: pair counting and the first configurational correction

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: The logarithm and beta derivative are complete, and the correction is visibly reorganized as an extensive energy per particle.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The total energy is N times an energy per molecule.
assets.caption_hint: interaction correction to energy in extensive form

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_09.png
assets.rationale: The pressure derivative and positive quadratic-density correction are simultaneously visible and unobstructed.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Differentiate log Z with respect to volume to obtain pressure.
assets.caption_hint: pressure correction from the volume derivative of log Z

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_10.png
assets.rationale: The attractive and repulsive potential profiles are legible and the lecturer does not cover the curves or their relation to the pressure sign.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The integrated potential may be positive or negative.
assets.caption_hint: qualitative attractive and repulsive pair potentials

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_11.png
assets.rationale: The scalar-function differential and mixed-partial condition are shown together in their most complete board state.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: An exact differential comes from a function of the coordinates.
assets.caption_hint: gradient differential and the mixed-partial exactness test

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_12.png
assets.rationale: Both the exact and inexact examples and their unequal cross derivatives are visible; the frame is clearer than adjacent lecturer-obstructed candidates.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: One choice integrates to xy; changing a sign makes the curl nonzero.
assets.caption_hint: worked exact and inexact one-form examples

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_13.png
assets.rationale: The piston sketch and the complete first-law relation occupy the same frame, directly matching the transition back to thermodynamics.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The energy differential contains work and reversible heat.
assets.caption_hint: piston work and the thermodynamic fundamental relation

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_14.png
assets.rationale: The heat one-form and both hypothetical partial derivatives are visible at the exact point where the curl test is set up.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: If heat were a function, its mixed derivatives would agree.
assets.caption_hint: heat one-form and its hypothetical exactness conditions

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_15.png
assets.rationale: The ideal-gas pressure and energy equations are centered, fully legible, and free of lecturer obstruction.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: For the ideal gas, pressure is two thirds of energy density.
assets.caption_hint: ideal-gas relation between pressure and energy

assets.name: lecture_06_figure_16.png
assets.rationale: The final nonzero pressure derivative is complete and appears beside the heat one-form, making the inexactness conclusion visually explicit.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The pressure derivative with respect to energy is not zero.
assets.caption_hint: failed exactness condition for heat in an ideal gas
